_encyclopedia.Western Heat Dome Mar 20 - The Peak (202:
Western Heat Dome: 2026-03-20 -- The Peak

What Happened
The event reached its absolute apex. Four stations in Arizona and California hit 112F -- Martinez Lake AZ, Fort Yuma AZ, Squaw Lake CA, and Buttercup CA -- setting the all-time US temperature record for March, just 1F below the all-time April record. Phoenix hit 105F, the earliest such reading by more than a month. San Francisco reached 90F, breaking an all-time March record that had stood since records began in 1874 -- 152 years. Eight states set all-time March records on this single day.

Climate Attribution
Climate Shift Index: Level 5 (maximum). World Weather Attribution conducted a rapid analysis and classified this event as "virtually impossible" without human-induced climate change -- a 1-in-500-year event in the current climate, 800 times more likely due to fossil fuel burning. The anthropogenic signal added at least 4.7F (2.6C) to the heat. CSI 5 means the anthropogenic signal is not a contributing factor but the dominant cause.

Earth System Context
Climate Change: The WWA finding -- "virtually impossible" without climate change -- places this event in the category of phenomena that exist only because the Earth system has been shifted. The 1954 Yuma record was set in a climate with ~315 ppm CO2. The 2026 record was set at ~427 ppm. The additional energy trapped by that difference is what made this event possible. The new national March record of 112F came within 1F of the April record (113F, Death Valley 1946/2012) -- the calendar distinction between March and April weather is dissolving.

Freshwater Change: Denver recorded 85F, 30F above normal. The Rocky Mountain snowpack that supplies the Colorado, Platte, and Arkansas river systems is under direct assault. Snowpack provides 75% of Western water supply. Early melt does not just shift timing -- rapid melt overwhelms reservoirs, causes flooding, and the water that runs off in March is not available in August when demand peaks.

Land System Change: Wildfire preconditioning is now severe. The combination of early heat and wind desiccation has reduced fuel moisture across Southern California chaparral and Arizona grasslands to levels normally seen in late May. Any ignition source -- lightning, powerline, human -- would find receptive fuels.

Novel Entities (Energy System Feedback): Early-season AC demand is spiking across the Southwest grid. Utilities planned for spring maintenance outages on generation assets -- those outages are being cancelled. Peaking plants (typically gas-fired) are coming online months early, adding CO2 emissions that reinforce the warming that caused the event. This is the feedback loop: heat drives energy demand drives emissions drives heat.

Record-Breaking Stations (as of 2026-03-20)
Phoenix AZ early: 95F (+17F) -- NWS issues first Extreme Heat Watch
Yuma AZ early: 98F (+16F) -- Already tracking 15+ above normal
Palm Springs CA: 96F (+16F) -- Coachella Valley heating up early
Las Vegas NV early: 92F (+22F) -- Heat dome compressing over Great Basin
Thermal CA: 100F (+18F) -- First triple digits in Salton Sea basin
Tucson AZ: 97F (+21F) -- Southern AZ corridor heating
Phoenix AZ record: 101F (+23F) -- Earliest 100+ day EVER recorded in Phoenix
Las Vegas NV record: 94F (+24F) -- Shatters all-time March high
Death Valley CA: 108F (+22F) -- Earliest 105+ in Death Valley
Yuma AZ record: 109F (+27F) -- Broke 1954 record of 108F
Martinez Lake AZ: 112F (+32F) -- US March record (tied with Buttercup/Squaw Lake CA)
Phoenix AZ peak: 105F (+27F) -- Earliest 105F on record -- by more than a month
Buttercup CA: 112F (+30F) -- Ties US March record; 1F below all-time April record
Cottonwood Cove NV: 104F (+29F) -- Nevada all-time March record
San Francisco CA: 90F (+28F) -- All-time March record; records since 1874 (152 years)

Data & Sources
Temperature data: ERA5 reanalysis via CDS API when available; synthetic grid seeded with confirmed NWS records as fallback.
Attribution: World Weather Attribution rapid analysis (800x more likely, +4.7F/2.6C); Climate Central Climate Shift Index.
Planetary boundaries: Rockstrom et al. (2009), Richardson et al. (2023).
